input_text: Animals are either invertebrates or vertebrates. All animals with backbones reproduce by male-and-female mating. All vertebrate animals have a backbone. answer:

All vertebrate animals have a backbone. Harry doesn't have a backbone, so Harry is not a vertebrate.

Animals are either invertebrates or vertebrates. Harry is a bee (an animal), so Harry is either an invertebrate or a vertebrate. Since Harry is not a vertebrate, Harry is an invertebrate.

Now check the condition: "Harry is either both a vertebrate and an animal with a backbone, or neither a vertebrate nor an animal with a backbone."

Harry is not a vertebrate and not an animal with a backbone. So Harry is "neither a vertebrate nor an animal with a backbone" — the second part of the "either...or" is satisfied.

Therefore the condition is TRUE, and the conclusion follows: Harry is neither an invertebrate nor a queen bee.

But we established Harry IS an invertebrate. This creates a contradiction — the conclusion says Harry is not an invertebrate, but the premises establish Harry is an invertebrate.
